why_it_matters: Without trustworthy records and telemetry, you can’t prove what happened, learn from it, or meet legal/regulatory duties. Auditability underpins every other control.
wef_quote: Cyber resilience goes beyond cybersecurity; it minimizes the impact on primary goals.
actions: Standardize log policies and retention; centralize high-fidelity logs/metrics/traces; map evidence to controls and table-top scenarios; protect logs from tampering; automate audit pack generation for incidents and DR tests
metrics: Log coverage %; evidence completeness; % critical systems with immutable logging; audit finding closure time
evidence: SIEM/Splunk indexes; retention configs; immutability controls; audit trails; post-incident reviews

why_it_matters: Elastic capacity absorbs shocks and demand spikes so incidents don’t cascade into outages or SLO breaches.
wef_quote: Design to absorb and recover from events; avoid single points of failure.
actions: Set SLOs/error budgets; run capacity tests and game-days; autoscale critical paths; maintain warm DR capacity; predefine traffic-shedding and degraded-mode playbooks
metrics: Peak-to-average utilization; autoscale success rate; error budget burn; DR failover RTO/RPO attainment
evidence: Capacity tests; ITSI/Splunk KPIs; autoscaler configs; DR runbooks and reports; synthetic load outputs

why_it_matters: Outages erode trust and revenue; resilient services protect primary goals even when components fail or are attacked.
wef_quote: There is no such thing as 100% cybersecurity; act on the basis that incidents will occur.
actions: Prioritize crown-jewel services; implement redundancy/segmentation; backups with regular restores; chaos/DR exercises; incident comms templates; supplier dependency mapping and containment plans
metrics: SLO attainment; MTBF/MTTR; backup restore success; % critical services with multi-region failover
evidence: BCP/DR test reports; failover logs; backup/restore records; dependency maps; tabletop outcomes

why_it_matters: Resilience must be economically sustainable. Automation and shared data reduce downtime costs and toil.
wef_quote: Resilient organizations save significant downtime costs annually.
actions: Automate common responses (SOAR/autoremediation); decommission redundant tech; use FinOps on data and infra; prioritize fixes by business impact; measure cost of downtime and of change
metrics: Annual downtime cost; % workflows automated; mean cost per incident; data/platform spend vs ROI
evidence: SOAR playbooks; MTTx trends; FinOps reports; incident cost models; value assessments

why_it_matters: High-quality software and observability reduce incidents and shrink blast radius, improving customer experience.
wef_quote: Use data to detect minor issues before they escalate.
actions: Shift-left testing and SAST/DAST; golden signals dashboards; SLO-driven release gates; progressive delivery with canaries; post-incident reviews feed backlog prioritization
metrics: Change failure rate; 95p/99p latency; error rates; % releases with canary; escaped defect rate
evidence: APM traces; Synthetics; CI/CD logs; release notes; PIR action trackers

why_it_matters: Security incidents are inevitable; resilience limits business impact and protects safety in IT and OT.
wef_quote: Prepare to anticipate, withstand, recover and adapt in a contested environment.
actions: Crown-jewel threat modelling; MFA/segmentation/hardening; threat intel + detection engineering; purple-team exercises; incident response runbooks with legal/comms; OT-specific safeguards and drills
metrics: MTTD/MTTR; containment time; % high-risk controls tested; phishing/reporting rates; tabletop frequency
evidence: SOC detections; SOAR runs; IR playbooks; red/purple team reports; OT safety cases

why_it_matters: Humans run the system. Clear, usable processes and tooling reduce error rates and speed response under stress.
wef_quote: Build a common language and psychological safety to increase timely reporting.
actions: Runbooks with one-page quick starts; pre-approved break-glass; human-factors reviews after incidents; golden paths for ops; simplify on-call with clear ownership; regular tabletop exercises with business
metrics: Time to execute runbook; handoff errors; % services with clear owners; training coverage; ticket reopen rate
evidence: Runbooks; RACI; tabletop notes; learning reviews; on-call rosters

why_it_matters: Markets and threats change. Adaptive organizations learn from incidents and evolve faster than adversaries.
wef_quote: Learn from incidents and adapt to strengthen the posture — perhaps find better ways to deliver value.
actions: Blameless learning reviews; track learn→change lead time; architecture fitness functions; modular designs with well-defined contracts; partner exercises across the ecosystem
metrics: Mean time to learn→ship fix; % services with contract tests; pace of safe change; partner exercise cadence
evidence: Learning review backlog links; ADRs; service contracts; ecosystem exercise reports
